manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

method: Verified records against arXiv Atom metadata and independently opened the arXiv HTML full-text endpoints. Labels describe evidence inspected, not merely the abstract record.

sources.title: HypRQ-VAE: Hyperbolic Item Indexing for Long-Tail-Aware Generative Recommender Systems

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — frames sequential recommendation as user behavior represented by item-ID sequences; generative recommendation predicts items.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: YES — proposes Hyperbolic Residual-Quantized VAE item indexing in hyperbolic space.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: YES — hyperbolic item indices/SIDs are used by generative recommendation.

sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses all three requested components: sequential user behavior, hyperbolic item indexing, and generative item identifiers. The abstract and full-text HTML identify HypRQ-VAE as hyperbolic item indexing for generative recommenders, and discuss sequential recommendation/user behavior item sequences.
sources.qualification: The work is listed as accepted for ICDM 2026 by its arXiv record; this is an arXiv preprint, not evidence of a DOI assignment. Full-text HTML was directly accessible and checked.

sources.title: HMamba: Hyperbolic Mamba for Sequential Recommendation

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — sequential recommendation and temporal evolution of user preferences/interaction sequences.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: NO evidence found — paper describes hyperbolic Mamba sequence modeling, not semantic-ID generation.

sources.exact_overlap: Evidence for the behavioral-sequential + hyperbolic pair only; it is not an all-three intersection source.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — predicts the next item from items in a user session.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: NO evidence found — method uses semantic codeword tuples; no hyperbolic geometry claim in inspected text.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: YES — semantically meaningful codeword tuples are Semantic IDs generated autoregressively.

sources.exact_overlap: Foundational direct evidence for next-item behavior + generative semantic IDs, but not hyperbolic geometry. NeurIPS 2023 per arXiv record.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Hypergraphs for Sequential Recommendation

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — sequential recommendation modeling user/item interactions and temporal dynamics.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: NO evidence in abstract — embeddings/recommendation architecture, not generative semantic IDs.

sources.exact_overlap: Behavior + hyperbolic recommendation evidence only. Abstract inspected; full-text content was not inspected, so absence of SID evidence is limited to abstract.

sources.title: Poincaré Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks for Sequential Recommendation

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — explicitly models sequential patterns from user behavior evolution.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: YES — Poincaré ball representations and hyperbolic operators.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: NO evidence in abstract — no semantic-ID generative retrieval described.

sources.exact_overlap: Behavior + hyperbolic sequential recommendation evidence only. Abstract inspected; do not infer full-text absence of semantic IDs.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Long-tail/niche next-item behavior under sparse interaction histories
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: HypRQ-VAE (FULL_TEXT) directly links hyperbolic indexing to the power-law/long-tail structure and reports tail-item recommendation; TIGER (FULL_TEXT) reports improved retrieval for items with no prior interaction history.
behavior_problem_candidates.research_gap: Test whether hyperbolic semantic-ID code assignment improves behavior-conditioned next-item prediction for sparse/tail users and items over Euclidean SID baselines, separating item-indexing gains from sequence-model gains.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Preserving hierarchical and temporal preference structure in next-item prediction
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: HMamba and PHGR/H2SeqRec address hierarchical/temporal structure in sequential behavior with hyperbolic representations; TIGER supplies autoregressive SID next-item generation, but the cited sources do not jointly establish this combination apart from HypRQ-VAE's broader intersection.
behavior_problem_candidates.evidence_label: FULL_TEXT for HMamba/TIGER; ABSTRACT for PHGR/H2SeqRec
behavior_problem_candidates.research_gap: Evaluate whether hyperbolic geometry should parameterize semantic-ID construction, user-state representation, or both, using time-aware next-item metrics and hierarchy-sensitive analyses.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Reducing mismatch between user behavior sequences and generated item identifiers
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: TIGER generates item Semantic IDs from session sequences; HypRQ-VAE brings hyperbolic item indexing to generative recommenders.
behavior_problem_candidates.research_gap: Measure validity/collision, semantic and behavioral neighborhood preservation, and next-item ranking jointly; do not assume geometry improves user-state modeling merely because item indexing is hyperbolic.

limitations: Only HypRQ-VAE is a verified all-three intersection in the examined records. Its abstract/full-text HTML supports the overlap, but this search does not establish that it is the only such work globally.

The explicit full-text checks were arXiv HTML for HypRQ-VAE, HMamba, and TIGER. H2SeqRec and PHGR evidence here is abstract-level only; their lack of semantic-ID terminology is not a full-text negative finding.
No DOI was verified for the listed arXiv records; arXiv identifiers and canonical record links are provided instead. Do not invent DOI values.
HypRQ-VAE is very recent (September 2026) and listed as accepted for ICDM 2026. Independent replication, peer-reviewed version metadata, and long-term impact are not assessed.
This report uses published research sources only and does not use or infer any prior-candidate prompts or unseen future/test interactions.
